subproblems.title: Calculus of integer multiplicity representations: tangent locality, restriction, differences, orientation bound (accepted theorem cmc_imRep_locality_restrict_sub, reused)
subproblems.statement: (a) Let P, n ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P open and M ⊆ M' ⊆ U Borel sets with Hⁿ(M' ∩ K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ U (Hⁿ = μHE[n]). Then for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M and every linear subspace Q, M has approximate tangent space Q at x (SimonGMT HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q, Simon Ch. 3, 1.4) if and only if M' does. (b) If U ⊆ ℝ^P is open, R = (M, θ, ξ) is an IMRep in U (contract structure) and E is Borel, then (M ∩ E, θ, ξ) is an IMRep in U and it represents some current in 𝒟_n(U). (c) If U is open and A, B ∈ 𝒟_n(U) are integer multiplicity (contract IsIntegerMultiplicity), then so is A − B. (d) For every IMRep R in any U, for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ R.carrier, |R.orient(x)(α)| ≤ |α| for every n-covector α (|·| the Euclidean coefficient norm).

This is the comparator-accepted theorem of DAG node root.compactness_of_minimizing_currents-a1.im_calculus-a1 (Submission.cmc_imRep_locality_restrict_sub, candidate 2af75d6), reused with its byte-identical frozen type. Its proof is exactly Part (IMC) of the parent proof, reproduced here verbatim.
Part (IMC). Hⁿ:=μHE[n]; IMReps are written (carrier, mult, orient)=(M,θ,ξ); η_{x,r}(y):=r⁻¹(y−x) (blowUpMap); 𝒯(N,x,Q):=HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n N x Q; 𝒰(ζ,Q):=IsUnitOrientationOf ζ Q.
(P0) SimonGMT's density theorems use simonHausdorffOuterMeasureReal n=μHE[n] (n∈ℕ), so null sets, finiteness and densities transfer; Hⁿ is Borel regular.
(P1) Hⁿ(η_{x,r}(A))=r^{−n}Hⁿ(A) for all A (scaling, isometry invariance), so ∫_{η_{x,r}(A)}f dHⁿ=r^{−n}∫_Af∘η_{x,r}dHⁿ for Borel A, bounded Borel f.
(P2) (simon_theorem_3_6 with (P0)) If D is Borel, Hⁿ(D)<∞, then Hⁿ(D∩B̄_r(x))/(ω_nrⁿ)→0 as r ↓ 0 for Hⁿ-a.e. x∉D.
(P3) (Cauchy–Binet) det(ABᵀ)=Σ_{I∈𝕀}det(A_I)det(B_I) for n×P matrices A, B (A_I: columns I of A): expanding det(ABᵀ) multilinearly in its columns Σ_kB_{jk}A_{·k}, terms with a repeated index vanish, and grouping the rest by the increasing rearrangement I (k=I∘σ) gives Σ_Idet(A_I)Σ_σsgn(σ)Π_jB_{j,I_{σ(j)}}=Σ_Idet(A_I)det(B_I). (n>P: 𝕀=∅, rank ABᵀ<n.)
(P4) If τ_1,…,τ_n are orthonormal and ⟨α,ζ⟩=±α(τ) for all n-covectors α, then |⟨α,ζ⟩|≤|α|: with A_{ik}:=⟨τ_i,e_k⟩, α(τ)=Σ_Idet(A_I)α(e_I) (multilinear, alternating), so by Cauchy–Schwarz and (P3) |α(τ)|≤|α|(Σ_Idet(A_I)²)^{1/2}=|α|det(AAᵀ)^{1/2}=|α|, as AAᵀ=(⟨τ_i,τ_j⟩)=id. (n=0: |α(∅)|=|α|.)
(P5) Orthonormal bases τ, τ' of an n-dimensional Q satisfy τ'_i=Σ_jO_{ij}τ_j, O orthogonal, so α(τ')=det(O)α(τ)=±α(τ) for alternating α. Hence 𝒰(ζ,Q)∧𝒰(ζ',Q) ⇒ ζ'=±ζ, and 𝒰(ζ,Q) ⇒ 𝒰(−ζ,Q).
(P6) For an IMRep (M,θ,ξ) in open U and compact K⊆U, Hⁿ(M∩K) ≤ ∫_{M∩K}θ dHⁿ < ∞ (θ≥1 on M).
(d) For Hⁿ-a.e. x∈R.carrier some Q has 𝒰(R.orient x, Q) (orientation field), i.e. ⟨α, R.orient x⟩=±α(τ) for an orthonormal τ and all α; so |R.orient x α|≤|α| by (P4).
(a) Let D:=M'∖M.
1. For R∈ℕ, U_R:={x∈U : |x|<R, infDist(x,ℝ^P∖U)>1/R} ({|x|<R} if U=ℝ^P) is open with compact closure in U, U_R ↑ U. D_R:=D∩U_R is Borel, Hⁿ(D_R)≤Hⁿ(M'∩closure U_R)<∞, so by (P2) some Hⁿ-null Z_R has Hⁿ(D_R∩B̄_r(x))=o(rⁿ) for x∉D_R∪Z_R. Let Z'⊇⋃_RZ_R be Borel, Hⁿ-null (P0). For x∈M∖Z' choose R, r₀>0 with B̄_{r₀}(x)⊆U_R; then x∉D_R (x∈M) and D∩B̄_r(x)=D_R∩B̄_r(x) for r<r₀, so Hⁿ(D∩B̄_r(x))=o(rⁿ).
2. Fix such x, a subspace Q, f∈C_c(ℝ^P) with spt f⊆B_ρ(0). For r<r₀/ρ, η_{x,r}(M), η_{x,r}(M') meet B_ρ(0) in sets of finite Hⁿ-measure (genuine Bochner integrals), η_{x,r}(M')=η_{x,r}(M)⊔η_{x,r}(D) (η_{x,r} injective), and by (P1)
 |∫_{η_{x,r}(M')}f dHⁿ − ∫_{η_{x,r}(M)}f dHⁿ| = |∫_{η_{x,r}(D)}f dHⁿ| ≤ |f|_∞r^{−n}Hⁿ(D∩B_{rρ}(x)) → 0.
So both families have the same limit as r→0⁺ or both have none, and finrank Q=n is common: 𝒯(M,x,Q)↔𝒯(M',x,Q) for x∈M∖Z' and all Q; M∩Z' is Hⁿ⌞M-null.
(b) For R=(M,θ,ξ) let R':=(M∩E,θ,ξ).
1. M∩E is Borel, ⊆U, countably n-rectifiable (subset of M); θ is measurable, >0 on M∩E, ∫_{M∩E∩K}θ dHⁿ ≤ ∫_{M∩K}θ dHⁿ < ∞ for compact K⊆U; ξ is a.e. strongly measurable for Hⁿ⌞(M∩E)≤Hⁿ⌞M.
2. By (P6) and (a) for M∩E⊆M⊆U, 𝒯(M∩E,x,Q)↔𝒯(M,x,Q) for Hⁿ-a.e. x∈M∩E and all Q, so the orientation field of R gives that of R'.
3. A(ω):=∫_{M∩E}θ⟨ω,ξ⟩dHⁿ (ω∈𝒟ⁿ(U)) is linear, the integrand being integrable: |θ⟨ω,ξ⟩|≤|ω|_∞θ1_{tsupport ω} Hⁿ-a.e. on M by (d), tsupport ω⊆U compact. If ω_j→0 in 𝒟ⁿ(U) (TestFormOnConverges: supports in a fixed compact K⊆U, all derivatives converge uniformly; so |ω_j|_∞→0, norms on covectors being equivalent), |A(ω_j)| ≤ |ω_j|_∞∫_{M∩K}θ dHⁿ → 0. So A is a GeometricCurrentOn U n represented by R' (IMRep.Represents).
(c) Let R_A=(M_A,θ_A,ξ_A), R_B=(M_B,θ_B,ξ_B) represent A, B.
1. Take Borel ξ̃_A, ξ̃_B equal to ξ_A, ξ_B Hⁿ-a.e. on M_A, resp. M_B (a.e. strong measurability), and 0 off them. Let G be the set of x∈M_A∪M_B such that: if x∈M_A, ξ̃_A(x)=ξ_A(x) and 𝒯(M_A,x,Q_A(x)), 𝒰(ξ_A x,Q_A(x)) for some Q_A(x); likewise for B; and 𝒯(N,x,·)↔𝒯(N',x,·) if x∈N, (N,N')∈{(M_A∩M_B,M_A), (M_A∩M_B,M_B)}. By the orientation fields, (P6) and (a), (M_A∪M_B)∖G is Hⁿ-null; let N₀ be a Borel Hⁿ-null superset (P0).
2. For x∈(M_A∩M_B)∖N₀, 𝒯(M_A∩M_B,x,Q) for Q=Q_A(x) and Q=Q_B(x) (def. of G), so Q_A(x)=Q_B(x) (HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt.unique) and by (P5) ξ̃_B(x)=ε(x)ξ̃_A(x), where ε(x):=1 if ξ̃_B(x)=ξ̃_A(x), −1 otherwise (Borel).
3. Let O:=(M_A∩M_B)∖N₀, k:=θ_A−εθ_B∈ℤ on O,

For x∉N₀, θ1_Mζ = θ_A1_{M_A}ξ̃_A − θ_B1_{M_B}ξ̃_B (on O: if k=0 both vanish, else θ_Aξ̃_A − θ_Bεξ̃_A=kξ̃_A=|k|sign(k)ξ̃_A; other cases immediate).
4. For ω∈𝒟ⁿ(U), pairing with ω and integrating (N₀ null; integrable by (d), θ1_M≤θ_A1_{M_A}+θ_B1_{M_B}): ∫_Mθ⟨ω,ζ⟩dHⁿ = ∫_{M_A}θ_A⟨ω,ξ_A⟩dHⁿ − ∫_{M_B}θ_B⟨ω,ξ_B⟩dHⁿ = (A−B)(ω).
5. M is Borel, ⊆M_A∪M_B⊆U, countably n-rectifiable (countable unions, subsets); θ≥1 on M (|k|≥1 where k≠0), ∫_{M∩K}θ ≤ ∫_{M_A∩K}θ_A+∫_{M_B∩K}θ_B < ∞ for compact K⊆U; ζ is Borel, so a.e. strongly measurable.
6. By (P6), Hⁿ(M∩K)≤Hⁿ(M_A∩K)+Hⁿ(M_B∩K)<∞ for compact K⊆U, so (a) applies to M∩M_A⊆M_A, M∩M_A⊆M, M∩M_B⊆M_B, M∩M_B⊆M: for Hⁿ-a.e. x∈M∩M_A, 𝒯(M,x,·)↔𝒯(M∩M_A,x,·)↔𝒯(M_A,x,·), likewise for M_B. For such x∉N₀: if x∈M_A, 𝒯(M,x,Q_A(x)) and ζ(x)=±ξ_A(x) (cases M_A∖M_B, O; ξ̃_A(x)=ξ_A(x)); if x∈M_B∖M_A, 𝒯(M,x,Q_B(x)) and ζ(x)=−ξ_B(x); so 𝒰(ζ(x),Q_A(x)), resp. 𝒰(ζ(x),Q_B(x)), by (P5). So the orientation field holds a.e. on M, and (M,θ,ζ) is an IMRep in U representing A−B, so A−B is integer multiplicity.

(b): all IMRep fields restrict; the orientation field transfers by (a); continuity of the restricted current from local integrability and (d).

subproblems.title: Evaluation bound |T(ω)| ≤ r·M_W(T) when tsupport ω ⊆ W and |ω| ≤ r (parent fact (E1); accepted theorem cmr_abs_apply_le_massOn, reused)
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let U, W ⊆ ℝ^P be arbitrary sets, let T ∈ 𝒟_n(U) (GeometricCurrentOn U n), ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) (TestFormOn U n) and r ∈ ℝ. Write |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α and M_W(T) := T.massOn W ∈ [0, ∞]. By Simon 6.2.5, M_W(T) is the supremum of ofReal T(φ) over φ ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) with tsupport φ ⊆ W and |φ(x)| ≤ 1 for all x. If M_W(T) ≠ ∞, tsupport ω ⊆ W and |ω(x)| ≤ r for every x ∈ ℝ^P, then |T(ω)| ≤ r·(M_W(T)).toReal.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U W : Set (Euclid P)) (T : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (ω : TestFormOn U n) (r : ℝ), T.massOn W ≠ ∞ → tsupport (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) ⊆ W → (∀ x, covectorEuclideanNorm ((ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) x) ≤ r) → |T ω| ≤ r * (T.massOn W).toReal
subproblems.natural_proof:
This is the comparator-accepted theorem of DAG node root.compactness_of_minimizing_currents-a1.mass_representation-a1.eval_mass_bound-a1 (Submission.cmr_abs_apply_le_massOn), reused with its identical frozen type. Source: parent proof, elementary fact (E1), with an arbitrary bound r in place of |ω|_∞.
1. (Homogeneity.) Let t ∈ ℝ and α be an n-covector. Then (t•α)(e_I) = t·α(e_I) for every I : Fin n → Fin P, so Σ_I [StrictMono I]((t•α)(e_I))² = t²·S with S := Σ_I [StrictMono I](α(e_I))² ≥ 0. Hence |t•α| = √(t²S) = |t|·√S = |t|·|α|. Also |α| ≥ 0, being a square root, and |−α| = |α| (covectorEuclideanNorm_neg).
2. (r ≥ 0.) By hypothesis 0 ≤ |ω(0)| ≤ r.
3. Put M := T.massOn W and m := M.toReal ≥ 0. Since M ≠ ∞, for every real a, ENNReal.ofReal a ≤ M implies a ≤ m (ENNReal.ofReal_le_iff_le_toReal).
4. (Admissible rescalings.) Fix ε > 0 and let s := r + ε > 0. Let ω' := s⁻¹ • ω, an element of TestFormOn U n (a submodule) whose underlying form is x ↦ s⁻¹•ω(x). Then tsupport ω' ⊆ tsupport ω ⊆ W, since the tsupport of a scalar multiple is contained in the tsupport. By step 1, |ω'(x)| = s⁻¹|ω(x)| ≤ r/s ≤ 1 for all x. Hence ω' ∈ massAdmissibleOn U n W. Likewise −ω' ∈ massAdmissibleOn U n W, since it has the same tsupport and |−ω'(x)| = |ω'(x)|.
5. (Bound.) By GeometricCurrentOn.le_massOn, ofReal(T ω') ≤ M and ofReal(T(−ω')) ≤ M. By step 3, T ω' ≤ m and −T ω' = T(−ω') ≤ m (T is linear), i.e. |T ω'| ≤ m. By linearity T ω' = s⁻¹·T ω, so |T ω| = s·|T ω'| ≤ (r + ε)·m.
6. (Conclusion.) Since ε > 0 is arbitrary and m ≥ 0, |T ω| ≤ r·m = r·(T.massOn W).toReal.
proof_key_steps: For ε > 0, both ±(r+ε)⁻¹ω are admissible for M_W(T).
le_massOn and M_W(T) ≠ ∞ give |T ω| ≤ (r+ε)·M_W(T).toReal.
Let ε → 0.

subproblems.title: Covectors with the coefficient norm form a Euclidean space (accepted theorem cmr_covector_euclidean_equiv, reused)
subproblems.statement: For all P, n ∈ ℕ there are d ∈ ℕ and a continuous linear equivalence c from the space of n-covectors on ℝ^P (Covector (Euclid P) n, with its operator-norm topology) onto ℝ^d = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d) such that covectorEuclideanNorm α = ‖c(α)‖ for every n-covector α. Here covectorEuclideanNorm α = (Σ_{I strictly increasing} α(e_I)²)^{1/2}, with e_I = (e_{I(0)}, …, e_{I(n−1)}) for the standard basis e of ℝ^P.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ), ∃ (d : ℕ) (c : Covector (Euclid P) n ≃L[ℝ] EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)), ∀ α : Covector (Euclid P) n, covectorEuclideanNorm α = ‖c α‖
subproblems.natural_proof:
This is the comparator-accepted theorem of DAG node root.compactness_of_minimizing_currents-a1.mass_representation-a1.covector_euclidean_equiv-a1 (Submission.cmr_covector_euclidean_equiv), reused with its identical frozen type. Source: parent proof, Notation paragraph: c(α) := (α(e_I))_I is a linear isomorphism onto a Euclidean space with |α| = ‖c(α)‖, injective because alternating forms are determined by their values on increasing tuples of basis vectors.
1. Notation. Λ := Covector (Euclid P) n; J := Fin n → Fin P, a finite type; for I ∈ J, e_I := (fun i => EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin P) ℝ (I i)); F := EuclideanSpace ℝ J, a finite-dimensional real inner product space.
2. Coefficient map. Define A : Λ →ₗ[ℝ] F by A α := WithLp.toLp 2 (fun I => if StrictMono I then α e_I else 0). For each fixed I, α ↦ α e_I is additive and commutes with real scalars (it is evaluation of a continuous alternating map at a fixed tuple), so A is ℝ-linear.
3. Norm identity. By EuclideanSpace.norm_eq, ‖A α‖ = √(Σ_I ‖(A α) I‖²) = √(Σ_I (if StrictMono I then (α e_I)² else 0)). This uses ‖t‖² = t² for real t and (if p then a else 0)² = if p then a² else 0. The right-hand side is covectorEuclideanNorm α by definition.
4. Injectivity. Let A α = 0, i.e. α(e_I) = 0 for every strictly increasing I : Fin n → Fin P. Let v : Fin n → ℝ^P. Writing v_j = Σ_l v_j(l)·e_l (e_l := EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin P) ℝ l) and expanding by multilinearity in each of the n arguments gives α(v) = Σ_{J : Fin n → Fin P} (Π_j v_j(J j))·α(e_J). If J is not injective, e_J has two equal entries and α(e_J) = 0 because α is alternating. If J is injective, let σ := Tuple.sort J, a permutation of Fin n with J ∘ σ monotone (Tuple.monotone_sort); J ∘ σ is injective, hence strictly increasing, so α(e_{J∘σ}) = 0 by hypothesis, while α(e_{J∘σ}) = sign(σ)·α(e_J) (AlternatingMap.map_perm applied to the underlying alternating map of α). Hence α(e_J) = 0 for every J, so α(v) = 0 for every v and α = 0 (ContinuousAlternatingMap.ext). Thus A is injective.
5. Isometric identification of the range. Let S := LinearMap.range A, a subspace of F; with the induced inner product it is a finite-dimensional real inner product space. Let d := finrank ℝ S and b := stdOrthonormalBasis ℝ S, an orthonormal basis indexed by Fin d; b.repr : S ≃ₗᵢ[ℝ] EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d) is a linear isometric equivalence. Let e₀ := LinearEquiv.ofInjective A (using step 4), so e₀ : Λ ≃ₗ[ℝ] S and (e₀ α : F) = A α. Let c₀ := e₀.trans b.repr.toLinearEquiv. Then ‖c₀ α‖ = ‖b.repr (e₀ α)‖ = ‖e₀ α‖ = ‖A α‖ = covectorEuclideanNorm α, since the norm of an element of a subspace is its ambient norm.
6. Continuity. Λ is finite-dimensional, being linearly equivalent to EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d) via c₀ (LinearEquiv.finiteDimensional applied to c₀.symm). A linear equivalence between finite-dimensional real normed spaces is a homeomorphism, so c := c₀.toContinuousLinearEquiv : Λ ≃L[ℝ] EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d) is a continuous linear equivalence. It satisfies ‖c α‖ = ‖c₀ α‖ = covectorEuclideanNorm α for all α.
7. Conclusion. d and c satisfy the claim. Consequently |·| = covectorEuclideanNorm is a norm on Λ: |α + β| ≤ |α| + |β|, |tα| = |t||α|, |α| = 0 iff α = 0, and |·| is continuous.
proof_key_steps: The coefficient map A, sending α to α(e_I) on strictly increasing I and to 0 elsewhere, into EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n → Fin P) satisfies ‖Aα‖ = covectorEuclideanNorm α.
A is injective: multilinear expansion in the standard basis, alternation kills non-injective index maps, and sorting (sign of the permutation) reduces injective ones to strictly increasing ones.
range A ≅ ℝ^d isometrically via an orthonormal basis; compose with LinearEquiv.ofInjective.
Finite-dimensionality upgrades the linear equivalence to a continuous linear equivalence.

subproblems.title: Uniform smooth approximation of continuous unit covector fields (accepted theorem dor_ims_sua_mollify_unit_field, reused)
subproblems.statement: Let P, n be natural numbers, Λ := Covector (Euclid P) n with operator norm ‖·‖, and |·| := covectorEuclideanNorm. Let V ⊆ ℝ^P be open. Let g : ℝ^P → Λ be continuous with compact support, tsupport g ⊆ V and |g(x)| ≤ 1 for every x. Let ε > 0. Then there is an n-form ω : ℝ^P → Λ that is C^∞ with compact support (IsTestForm ω), with tsupport ω ⊆ V, |ω(x)| ≤ 1 for every x, and |ω(x) − g(x)| ≤ ε for every x ∈ ℝ^P.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (V : Set (Euclid P)) (g : Euclid P → Covector (Euclid P) n) (ε : ℝ), IsOpen V → Continuous g → HasCompactSupport g → tsupport g ⊆ V → (∀ x, covectorEuclideanNorm (g x) ≤ 1) → 0 < ε → ∃ ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n, IsTestForm ω ∧ tsupport ω ⊆ V ∧ (∀ x, covectorEuclideanNorm (ω x) ≤ 1) ∧ ∀ x, covectorEuclideanNorm (ω x - g x) ≤ ε
subproblems.natural_proof:
This is the comparator-accepted theorem of DAG node root.density_one_implies_regular-a1.imrep_mass_and_support-a1.smooth_unit_approximation-a1.mollify_unit_field-a1, reused with its identical frozen type. Its proof is reproduced here (mollification), with the coefficient isometry written out.
Notation: Λ := Covector (Euclid P) n with the operator norm ‖·‖; |·| := covectorEuclideanNorm; e_I := (e_{I 0}, …, e_{I(n−1)}) for the standard basis e of ℝ^P.
1. (Norm facts.) Let A : Λ → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n → Fin P), A α := (if StrictMono I then α(e_I) else 0)_I. A is linear and continuous, since |α(e_I)| ≤ ‖α‖. By the definition of covectorEuclideanNorm and EuclideanSpace.norm_eq, |α| = ‖A α‖. Let C₀ := ‖A‖. Then |α| ≤ C₀‖α‖, and |·| inherits the triangle inequality and homogeneity from the Euclidean norm.
2. (Support margin.) tsupport g is compact and contained in the open set V. So there is r > 0 with cthickening r (tsupport g) ⊆ V (IsCompact.exists_cthickening_subset_open).
3. (Uniform continuity.) g is continuous with compact support, hence uniformly continuous. Choose s₀ > 0 with ‖g(y) − g(x)‖ < ε/(C₀ + 1) whenever dist(y, x) < s₀, and put s := min(s₀, r) > 0.
4. (Kernel.) Let φ be a smooth bump on ℝ^P centred at 0 with inner radius s/2 and outer radius s (ContDiffBump). Then φ is C^∞, 0 ≤ φ ≤ 1, φ = 1 on closedBall(0, s/2) and support φ = ball(0, s). Its integral J := ∫ φ is positive (φ ≥ 0 and φ = 1 on a ball of positive measure) and finite. Then ψ := J⁻¹φ is C^∞, ψ ≥ 0, ∫ ψ = 1, support ψ = ball(0, s), and tsupport ψ = closedBall(0, s) is compact.
5. (Definition.) Let ω(x) := ∫ ψ(t)•g(x − t) dt, the convolution ψ ⋆ g. This is a Bochner integral in the complete space Λ, and for each x the integrand is continuous with compact support in t.
6. (Smoothness.) ψ is C^∞ with compact support and g is continuous, hence locally integrable. So ω is C^∞ (HasCompactSupport.contDiff_convolution_left).
7. (Support.) support ω ⊆ support ψ + support g ⊆ thickening(s, tsupport g). Hence tsupport ω ⊆ cthickening(s, tsupport g) ⊆ cthickening(r, tsupport g) ⊆ V, and ω has compact support (HasCompactSupport.convolution). So IsTestForm ω and tsupport ω ⊆ V.
8. (|ω| ≤ 1.) A commutes with the Bochner integral (ContinuousLinearMap.integral_comp_comm). So |ω(x)| = ‖A ω(x)‖ = ‖∫ ψ(t)·A(g(x − t)) dt‖ ≤ ∫ ψ(t)|g(x − t)| dt ≤ ∫ ψ = 1.
9. (Approximation.) Since ∫ ψ = 1, ω(x) − g(x) = ∫ ψ(t)•(g(x − t) − g(x)) dt. Here ψ(t) ≠ 0 only when ‖t‖ < s ≤ s₀, and then ‖g(x − t) − g(x)‖ < ε/(C₀ + 1). Hence ‖ω(x) − g(x)‖ ≤ ε/(C₀ + 1), and by step 1, |ω(x) − g(x)| ≤ C₀ε/(C₀ + 1) ≤ ε.
10. Steps 6–9 show that ω is C^∞ with compact support, tsupport ω ⊆ V, |ω| ≤ 1 everywhere and |ω − g| ≤ ε everywhere.
proof_key_steps: The coefficient map A gives |α| = ‖Aα‖ ≤ ‖A‖·‖α‖.
Choose r > 0 with cthickening(r, tsupport g) ⊆ V; by uniform continuity choose 0 < s ≤ r with ‖g(y) − g(x)‖ < ε/(‖A‖+1) whenever dist(y, x) < s.
Convolve g with a normalized smooth bump ψ of radius s: ω = ψ ⋆ g is C^∞ with compact support and tsupport ω ⊆ cthickening(s, tsupport g) ⊆ V.
A commutes with the integral, so |ω(x)| ≤ ∫ ψ(t)|g(x − t)| dt ≤ 1.

subproblems.title: L¹ approximation of bounded measurable covector fields by unit test forms (accepted theorem rsd_mw_exists_testForm_approx, reused)
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let ν be a finite Borel measure on ℝ^P, let V ⊆ ℝ^P be open with ν(ℝ^P ∖ V) = 0, and let β : ℝ^P → Covector (Euclid P) n be ν-integrable with covectorEuclideanNorm (β x) ≤ 1 for ν-a.e. x. Then for every ε > 0 there is a smooth compactly supported n-form ω on ℝ^P (IsTestForm ω) with tsupport ω ⊆ V, covectorEuclideanNorm (ω x) ≤ 1 for every x, and ∫⁻ ofReal(covectorEuclideanNorm (ω x − β x)) dν(x) < ofReal ε.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (ν : Measure (Euclid P)) (V : Set (Euclid P)) (β : Euclid P → Covector (Euclid P) n), IsFiniteMeasure ν → IsOpen V → ν Vᶜ = 0 → Integrable β ν → (∀ᵐ x ∂ν, covectorEuclideanNorm (β x) ≤ 1) → ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∃ ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n, IsTestForm ω ∧ tsupport ω ⊆ V ∧ (∀ x, covectorEuclideanNorm (ω x) ≤ 1) ∧ ∫⁻ x, ENNReal.ofReal (covectorEuclideanNorm (ω x - β x)) ∂ν < ENNReal.ofReal ε
subproblems.natural_proof:
This is the comparator-accepted theorem of DAG node root.regular_set_dense-a1.mass_eq_weight-a1.test_form_approx-a1, reused with its identical frozen type. Its proof is reproduced here.
Notation. F := Covector (Euclid P) n with its operator norm ‖·‖, a complete normed space; N := covectorEuclideanNorm; 𝓘 := the strictly increasing I : Fin n → Fin P; e_I := (e_{I(0)}, …, e_{I(n−1)}); m := ν(ℝ^P) < ∞. 'a.e.' refers to ν.
1. Properties of N. N(α) = ‖c(α)‖₂ with c(α) := (α(e_I))_{I∈𝓘} linear, so N is a seminorm. Since |α(e_I)| ≤ ‖α‖, N(α) ≤ C‖α‖ with C := (#𝓘)^{1/2}. Hence |N(α) − N(α')| ≤ C‖α − α'‖, and N is continuous.
2. Compact core. For j ≥ 1 let K_j := {y : ‖y‖ ≤ j and ball(y, 1/j) ⊆ V}. The set {y : ball(y, r) ⊆ V} is closed, so each K_j is closed and bounded, hence compact. Also K_j ⊆ V, K_j ⊆ K_{j+1}, and ⋃_j K_j = V because V is open. Since ν is finite and ν(ℝ^P ∖ V) = 0, ν(ℝ^P ∖ K_j) = ν(V ∖ K_j) → 0. Fix K := K_j with ν(ℝ^P ∖ K) < ε/8.
3. Continuous approximation. ν is a finite Borel measure on ℝ^P, hence regular, and continuous compactly supported maps are dense in L¹(ν; F). So there is a continuous compactly supported g : ℝ^P → F with ∫ ‖g − β‖ dν ≤ ε/(8(C + 1)).
4. Retraction. Let π(a) := max(1, N(a))⁻¹•a. Then π is continuous, π(0) = 0 and N(π(a)) ≤ 1. Moreover N(π(a) − b) ≤ 2N(a − b) whenever N(b) ≤ 1: if N(a) ≤ 1 then π(a) = a; otherwise N(a − π(a)) = N(a) − 1 ≤ N(a) − N(b) ≤ N(a − b), and the triangle inequality gives the bound. Put g₁ := π∘g. Then g₁ is continuous with compact support, N(g₁) ≤ 1, and N(g₁ − β) ≤ 2C‖g − β‖ a.e.
5. Smoothing. Let η := ε/(8(C + 1)(m + 1)). g₁ is uniformly continuous, so convolution with a smooth mollifier of small radius gives a C^∞ map g₂' with ‖g₂'(x) − g₁(x)‖ < η for all x. Put g₂ := (1 + Cη)⁻¹•g₂'. Then g₂ is C^∞, N(g₂) ≤ 1, and N(g₂ − g₁) ≤ 2Cη.
6. Cut-off. Choose an open V₀ with K ⊆ V₀ whose closure is compact and contained in V. By the smooth Urysohn lemma there is a C^∞ function χ : ℝ^P → [0, 1] with χ = 1 on K and tsupport χ ⊆ closure V₀. Then ω := χ•g₂ is C^∞ with compact support, tsupport ω ⊆ V, and N(ω) ≤ 1 everywhere.
7. Estimate. Almost everywhere: on K, N(ω − β) ≤ 2Cη + 2C‖g − β‖; off K, N(ω − β) ≤ N(ω) + N(β) ≤ 2. Integrating, ∫⁻ ofReal N(ω − β) dν ≤ ofReal(2Cηm + 2C∫‖g − β‖ dν) + 2ν(ℝ^P ∖ K) < ofReal(ε/2) + ofReal(ε/4) ≤ ofReal ε.
Hence ω has all the required properties.
proof_key_steps: N = covectorEuclideanNorm is a continuous seminorm with N ≤ C‖·‖.
Inner regularity: a compact K ⊆ V with ν(ℝ^P ∖ K) < ε/8.
L¹ density gives a continuous compactly supported g with ∫‖g − β‖ dν small.
The radial retraction gives g₁ = π∘g with N(g₁) ≤ 1 and N(g₁ − β) ≤ 2C‖g − β‖ a.e.
A smooth uniform approximation, rescaled, gives g₂ with N(g₂) ≤ 1 and N(g₂ − g₁) ≤ 2Cη.
A smooth cut-off χ = 1 on K gives ω = χ·g₂, and splitting over K and its complement gives the L¹ estimate.

subproblems.title: Coordinate covectors dx^I = det(v_j(I k)) exist and span (parent Notation paragraph)
subproblems.statement: For all P, n ∈ ℕ: (a) for every I : Fin n → Fin P there is an n-covector θ on ℝ^P with θ(v) = det(v_j(I k))_{k,j} for every v : Fin n → ℝ^P, i.e. the determinant of the n×n matrix Matrix.of fun k j => v j (I k); (b) let ζ be an n-vector (MultiVector P n, a continuous linear functional on n-covectors) such that ζ(θ) = 0 whenever I : Fin n → Fin P is strictly increasing and θ is an n-covector with θ(v) = det(v_j(I k))_{k,j} for all v; then ζ = 0.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ), (∀ I : Fin n → Fin P, ∃ θ : Covector (Euclid P) n, ∀ v : Fin n → Euclid P, θ v = Matrix.det (Matrix.of fun k j => v j (I k))) ∧ ∀ ζ : MultiVector P n, (∀ (I : Fin n → Fin P) (θ : Covector (Euclid P) n), StrictMono I → (∀ v : Fin n → Euclid P, θ v = Matrix.det (Matrix.of fun k j => v j (I k))) → ζ θ = 0) → ζ = 0
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof, Notation paragraph: the alternating dx^I(v_1, …, v_n) := det((v_j)^{i_k})_{k,j} satisfies dx^I(e_J) = δ_{IJ}, and every covector is α = Σ_I α(e_I) dx^I; this is used in step 10 of the parent proof (ω = Σ_α ω_α dx^α).
Notation: e_i := EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin P) ℝ i = EuclideanSpace.single i 1, so e_i(l) = 1 if l = i and 0 otherwise; e_J := (fun j => e_{J j}); 𝓘 := the finset of strictly increasing J : Fin n → Fin P (classical decidability); |·| := covectorEuclideanNorm.
1. (Part (a).) Fix I. The map Θ : (Fin n → (Fin n → ℝ)) → ℝ, Θ(u) := det(Matrix.of fun k j => u j k), is multilinear and alternating in the family u. Indeed it is the determinant of the matrix whose j-th column is u j, i.e. of the transpose of the matrix with rows u j; since det Mᵀ = det M, Θ is Matrix.detRowAlternating, an alternating multilinear map. The coordinate map p_I : ℝ^P →ₗ[ℝ] (Fin n → ℝ), p_I x := (fun k => x (I k)), is linear. Hence θ⁰ := Θ.compLinearMap p_I is an alternating n-linear map ℝ^P → ℝ with θ⁰(v) = det(Matrix.of fun k j => v j (I k)). By the Leibniz formula and |x(l)| ≤ ‖x‖, |θ⁰(v)| ≤ Σ_σ Π_j |v_j(I(σ j))| ≤ n!·Π_j ‖v_j‖. So θ_I := AlternatingMap.mkContinuous θ⁰ (n!) (with this bound) is an n-covector with θ_I(v) = det(Matrix.of fun k j => v j (I k)) for all v.
2. (Kronecker property.) Let I, J be strictly increasing. Since (e_{J j})(I k) = if J j = I k then 1 else 0, θ_I(e_J) = det M with M k j := if J j = I k then 1 else 0.
 - If I = J, then M = 1, because J j = J k iff j = k by injectivity; so θ_I(e_J) = 1.
 - If I ≠ J, there is k₀ with I k₀ ∉ range J. Otherwise range I ⊆ range J; both ranges have exactly n elements (strictly increasing maps are injective), so range I = range J and hence I = J (two strictly increasing maps Fin n → Fin P with the same range are equal, StrictMono.range_inj_of_wellFoundedLT), a contradiction. Then row k₀ of M is zero, so θ_I(e_J) = 0 (Matrix.det_eq_zero_of_row_eq_zero).
 So θ_I(e_J) = δ_{IJ} for I, J ∈ 𝓘.
3. (Expansion.) Let α be an n-covector and α' := α − Σ_{I∈𝓘} α(e_I)•θ_I. For J ∈ 𝓘, α'(e_J) = α(e_J) − Σ_{I∈𝓘} α(e_I)·θ_I(e_J) = α(e_J) − α(e_J) = 0 by step 2. Every term of the sum defining |α'| therefore vanishes, so |α'| = 0. By the sibling covector_euclidean_equiv there are d and c : Covector (Euclid P) n ≃L[ℝ] EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d) with |β| = ‖c β‖ for all β. Thus c α' = 0 and α' = 0, since c is injective. Therefore α = Σ_{I∈𝓘} α(e_I)•θ_I.
4. (Part (b).) Let ζ satisfy the hypothesis of (b). For each I ∈ 𝓘 the covector θ_I of step 1 satisfies the determinant identity, hence ζ θ_I = 0. By step 3 and linearity, ζ α = Σ_{I∈𝓘} α(e_I)·ζ θ_I = 0 for every n-covector α. So ζ = 0 (ContinuousLinearMap.ext).
5. (Degenerate cases.) For n = 0, 𝓘 consists of the empty map and θ_∅ is the constant 1 (the determinant of the empty matrix). For n > P, 𝓘 = ∅ and step 3 shows that every n-covector vanishes. The argument covers both cases without change.
proof_key_steps: θ_I := det of the coordinate rows (I k), made continuous by the bound n!·Π‖v_j‖.
θ_I(e_J) = δ_IJ for strictly increasing I, J (a zero row when I ≠ J).
α − Σ_I α(e_I)θ_I has covectorEuclideanNorm 0, hence vanishes by covector_euclidean_equiv.
ζ vanishes on every θ_I, hence on every covector.

subproblems.title: Extension of T to compactly supported continuous coefficient fields (parent step 2)
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (T : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (d : ℕ) (c : Covector (Euclid P) n ≃L[ℝ] EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)), IsOpen U → (∀ W : Set (Euclid P), IsOpen W → CompactlyContained W U → T.massOn W < ∞) → (∀ α : Covector (Euclid P) n, covectorEuclideanNorm α = ‖c α‖) → ∃ L : CompactlySupportedContinuousMap U (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)) →ₗ[ℝ] ℝ, (∀ (ω : TestFormOn U n) (g : CompactlySupportedContinuousMap U (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d))), (∀ x : U, g x = c ((ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) x)) → L g = T ω) ∧ ∀ K : Set U, IsCompact K → ∃ M : ℝ, ∀ g : CompactlySupportedContinuousMap U (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)), tsupport g ⊆ K → (∀ x, ‖g x‖ ≤ 1) → |L g| ≤ M
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof, step 2 (extension of T to continuous forms by mollification, using (E1)). The coefficient space H := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d) and the isometry c are given as hypotheses. The mollification g_σ := g̃ ∗ φ_σ of the parent is supplied by the sibling mollify_unit_field, which normalizes a ContDiffBump kernel explicitly (Mathlib's ready-made normalized mollifier ContDiffBump.normed is outside the import closure of GMT.Ch07.Submission), and (E1) by the sibling eval_mass_bound.
Notation: Λ := Covector (Euclid P) n; |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α = ‖c α‖, so |·| is a norm on Λ (|α + β| ≤ |α| + |β|, |tα| = |t||α|); val : ↥U → ℝ^P is the inclusion, an embedding onto the open set U; 'W ⊂⊂ U' means CompactlyContained W U; M_W(T) := T.massOn W.
1. (Zero extension.) For g ∈ C_c(U, H) let S_g := val''(tsupport g), a compact subset of U. Define g̃ : ℝ^P → Λ by g̃(x) := c⁻¹(g⟨x, hx⟩) if x ∈ U and g̃(x) := 0 otherwise.
 - g̃ vanishes outside S_g: if x ∈ U ∖ S_g then ⟨x, hx⟩ ∉ tsupport g, so g̃(x) = c⁻¹(0) = 0.
 - g̃ is continuous. On the open set U it agrees with the continuous map c⁻¹ ∘ g ∘ (val restricted to U)⁻¹. On the open set ℝ^P ∖ S_g (S_g is compact, hence closed) it is 0. These two open sets cover ℝ^P.
 - Hence g̃ is continuous with compact support and tsupport g̃ ⊆ S_g ⊆ U.
 - |g̃(x)| = ‖g⟨x, hx⟩‖ for x ∈ U and 0 otherwise; (g₁ + g₂)~ = g̃₁ + g̃₂; (t g)~ = t g̃; S_{g₁+g₂} ⊆ S_{g₁} ∪ S_{g₂}; S_{tg} ⊆ S_g.
2. (Admissible open sets.) W is admissible for g if W is open, W ⊂⊂ U and S_g ⊆ W.
 - For every compact S ⊆ U there is an open W ⊂⊂ U with S ⊆ W. Choose δ > 0 with cthickening δ S ⊆ U (IsCompact.exists_cthickening_subset_open) and set W := thickening(δ/2) S. Then closure W ⊆ cthickening(δ/2) S, which is compact (a cthickening of a compact set in ℝ^P) and contained in U.
 - In particular admissible sets exist for every g, and for every compact K ⊆ ↥U there is an open W_K ⊂⊂ U with val''K ⊆ W_K.
 - If W₁, W₂ are open with W_i ⊂⊂ U, then W₁ ∪ W₂ is open and W₁ ∪ W₂ ⊂⊂ U, since the closure of a union of two sets is the union of the closures.
3. (Approximating sequences.) A sequence (ω_k) in TestFormOn U n approximates g on W with errors ε_k if tsupport ω_k ⊆ W and |ω_k(x) − g̃(x)| ≤ ε_k for all x and k, where ε_k → 0.
 - If W is admissible for g, such a sequence exists with ε_k = 1/(k+1). Let s := 1 + sup_x ‖g(x)‖, which is finite. The field s⁻¹g̃ is continuous with compact support, tsupport ⊆ S_g ⊆ W and |s⁻¹g̃| ≤ 1. The sibling mollify_unit_field (with V := W and ε := 1/(s(k+1))) gives a test form ω⁰_k with tsupport ω⁰_k ⊆ W, |ω⁰_k| ≤ 1 and |ω⁰_k − s⁻¹g̃| ≤ 1/(s(k+1)). Then ω_k := s•ω⁰_k is a test form with tsupport ⊆ W ⊆ U, so ω_k ∈ TestFormOn U n, and |ω_k − g̃| ≤ 1/(k+1).
 - If moreover ‖g(x)‖ ≤ 1 for all x, applying the sibling directly to g̃ gives such a sequence with, in addition, |ω_k(x)| ≤ 1 for all x and k.
4. (Cauchy estimate.) Let (ω_k) approximate g on W with errors ε_k and (ω'_k) approximate g on W' with errors ε'_k, where W and W' are admissible. W ∪ W' is open and ⊂⊂ U, so M := M_{W∪W'}(T) < ∞ by hypothesis. For all k, l, tsupport(ω_k − ω'_l) ⊆ W ∪ W' and |ω_k(x) − ω'_l(x)| ≤ ε_k + ε'_l. The sibling eval_mass_bound gives |T(ω_k) − T(ω'_l)| = |T(ω_k − ω'_l)| ≤ (ε_k + ε'_l)·M.toReal. Taking W' = W and ω' = ω shows that (T(ω_k))_k is a Cauchy sequence of reals, hence convergent. In general the estimate shows that the limits along (ω_k) and (ω'_k) coincide.
5. (Definition.) For each g choose an admissible W_g and an approximating sequence (ω^g_k) on W_g (steps 2–3), and set L(g) := lim_k T(ω^g_k). By step 4, L(g) = lim_k T(ω_k) for every sequence (ω_k) that approximates g on any admissible set.
6. (Linearity.) Let (ω_k) approximate g₁ on W₁ with errors ε_k, and (ω'_k) approximate g₂ on W₂ with errors ε'_k. Then (ω_k + ω'_k) approximates g₁ + g₂ on W₁ ∪ W₂ with errors ε_k + ε'_k; W₁ ∪ W₂ is admissible for g₁ + g₂ by steps 1–2. Also (t•ω_k) approximates t•g₁ on W₁ with errors |t|ε_k. By step 5 and linearity of T, L(g₁ + g₂) = lim_k T(ω_k + ω'_k) = L(g₁) + L(g₂) and L(t•g₁) = lim_k T(t•ω_k) = t·L(g₁). So L is a real linear map C_c(U, H) → ℝ.
7. (Property (i).) Let ω ∈ TestFormOn U n and g ∈ C_c(U, H) with g(x) = c(ω(x)) for all x ∈ ↥U.
 - g̃ = ω: for y ∈ U, g̃(y) = c⁻¹(c(ω(y))) = ω(y); for y ∉ U, ω(y) = 0 = g̃(y) because tsupport ω ⊆ U.
 - tsupport ω ⊆ S_g: support ω = val''(support g) ⊆ S_g because c is injective, and S_g is closed.
 - Hence for any admissible W the constant sequence ω_k := ω approximates g on W with errors 0, and L(g) = T(ω).
8. (Property (ii).) Let K ⊆ ↥U be compact, W_K as in step 2, and M := (M_{W_K}(T)).toReal, finite by hypothesis. Let g ∈ C_c(U, H) with tsupport g ⊆ K and ‖g‖ ≤ 1. Then S_g ⊆ val''K ⊆ W_K, so W_K is admissible for g. Step 3 gives an approximating sequence (ω_k) on W_K with |ω_k| ≤ 1. Both ω_k and −ω_k belong to massAdmissibleOn U n W_K. So ofReal(T ω_k) ≤ M_{W_K}(T) and ofReal(−T ω_k) ≤ M_{W_K}(T) (GeometricCurrentOn.le_massOn), i.e. |T(ω_k)| ≤ M. By step 5, |L(g)| = lim_k |T(ω_k)| ≤ M.
proof_key_steps: Extend g ∈ C_c(U, ℝ^d) by zero to the continuous compactly supported covector field g̃ = c⁻¹∘g, whose tsupport lies in the compact set S_g ⊆ U.
Admissible open sets W ⊂⊂ U containing S_g exist (thickenings) and are stable under finite unions.
mollify_unit_field gives test forms ω_k supported in W with |ω_k − g̃| ≤ 1/(k+1), and |ω_k| ≤ 1 when ‖g‖ ≤ 1.
eval_mass_bound on W ∪ W' makes T(ω_k) Cauchy with a limit independent of all choices; define L(g) as this limit.
Linearity follows from sums and scalings of approximating sequences; L(c∘ω) = T(ω) via the constant sequence; |L(g)| ≤ M_{W_K}(T) via the admissible forms ±ω_k.

subproblems.title: Riesz representation of locally bounded functionals on C_c(X, ℝ^d) (parent step 3)
subproblems.statement: Let X be a locally compact Hausdorff space with a countable basis, equipped with its Borel σ-algebra; let d ∈ ℕ. Let L be a real linear functional on C_c(X, ℝ^d) (CompactlySupportedContinuousMap X (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d))) that is locally bounded: for every compact K ⊆ X there is M ∈ ℝ with |L(g)| ≤ M for all g with tsupport g ⊆ K and ‖g(x)‖ ≤ 1 for all x. Then there are a Borel measure μ₀ on X that is finite on compact sets and a measurable map ν : X → ℝ^d that is μ₀-integrable on every compact set, such that L(g) = ∫ ⟨g(x), ν(x)⟩ dμ₀(x) for every g ∈ C_c(X, ℝ^d).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (X : Type) [TopologicalSpace X] [T2Space X] [LocallyCompactSpace X] [SecondCountableTopology X] [MeasurableSpace X] [BorelSpace X] (d : ℕ) (L : CompactlySupportedContinuousMap X (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)) →ₗ[ℝ] ℝ), (∀ K : Set X, IsCompact K → ∃ M : ℝ, ∀ g : CompactlySupportedContinuousMap X (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)), tsupport g ⊆ K → (∀ x, ‖g x‖ ≤ 1) → |L g| ≤ M) → ∃ (μ₀ : Measure X) (ν : X → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)), IsFiniteMeasureOnCompacts μ₀ ∧ Measurable ν ∧ (∀ K : Set X, IsCompact K → IntegrableOn ν K μ₀) ∧ ∀ g : CompactlySupportedContinuousMap X (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)), L g = ∫ x, inner ℝ (g x) (ν x) ∂μ₀
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof, step 3 (Riesz representation of the locally bounded functional L of step 2). The parent cites SimonGMT Chapter01 simon_theorem_4_14_caratheodory, which is not in the import closure of GMT.Ch07.Submission (verified: unknown identifier after `import GMT.Ch07.Submission`); the representation is therefore proved here directly. The argument uses only results that are in scope: Mathlib's scalar Riesz–Markov–Kakutani theorem (RealRMK.rieszMeasure, RealRMK.integral_rieszMeasure), CompactlySupportedContinuousMap.toRealPositiveLinear, and the Lebesgue decomposition.
Notation: H := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d); e_i := EuclideanSpace.single i 1 for i ∈ Fin d, so ⟨x, y⟩ = Σ_i x_i y_i; ‖f‖_∞ := sup_x |f(x)| for f ∈ C_c(X, ℝ), which is finite. X is σ-compact, being locally compact with a countable basis.
1. (Scalar functionals and their bound.) For i ∈ Fin d and f ∈ C_c(X, ℝ), the map f•e_i : x ↦ f(x)•e_i is continuous with support equal to support f, so it belongs to C_c(X, H). Then Λ_i(f) := L(f•e_i) defines a linear functional Λ_i on C_c(X, ℝ). Let K be compact and M_K as in the hypothesis; applying the hypothesis to g = 0 shows M_K ≥ 0.
 Claim (B): if tsupport f ⊆ K then |Λ_i(f)| ≤ M_K‖f‖_∞. If s := ‖f‖_∞ = 0 then f = 0. Otherwise g := (s⁻¹f)•e_i satisfies ‖g(x)‖ = |f(x)|/s ≤ 1 and tsupport g ⊆ K, so |L g| ≤ M_K, i.e. |Λ_i(f)| ≤ s·M_K.
2. (Variation.) For f ∈ C_c(X, ℝ≥0) let A_f := {h ∈ C_c(X, ℝ) : |h(x)| ≤ f(x) for all x} and V_i(f) := sup Λ_i(A_f). A_f contains 0. Every h ∈ A_f has support h ⊆ support f, hence tsupport h ⊆ tsupport f (a compact set), and ‖h‖_∞ ≤ ‖f‖_∞. By (B), Λ_i(A_f) is bounded above by M_{tsupport f}·‖f‖_∞. Properties:
 (a) V_i(f) ≥ 0 (take h = 0), and |Λ_i(f)| ≤ V_i(f) (take h = ±f, with f regarded as a real function).
 (b) V_i(t f) = t·V_i(f) for t ∈ ℝ≥0. For t = 0 only h = 0 qualifies. For t > 0, h ↦ t h is a bijection A_f → A_{tf} and Λ_i(t h) = tΛ_i(h).
 (c) V_i(f₁ + f₂) = V_i(f₁) + V_i(f₂).
  '≥': if h_j ∈ A_{f_j} then h₁ + h₂ ∈ A_{f₁+f₂}, so Λ_i(h₁) + Λ_i(h₂) ≤ V_i(f₁ + f₂); take suprema.
  '≤': let h ∈ A_{f₁+f₂}, h₁ := max(−f₁, min(h, f₁)) and h₂ := h − h₁. h₁ is continuous and vanishes where h does (f₁ ≥ 0), so h₁, h₂ ∈ C_c(X, ℝ), and |h₁| ≤ f₁. Pointwise |h₂| ≤ f₂: if |h| ≤ f₁ then h₂ = 0; if h > f₁ then 0 < h₂ = h − f₁ ≤ f₂; if h < −f₁ then 0 > h₂ = h + f₁ ≥ −f₂. So Λ_i(h) = Λ_i(h₁) + Λ_i(h₂) ≤ V_i(f₁) + V_i(f₂).
 Thus f ↦ V_i(f) is an ℝ≥0-linear map C_c(X, ℝ≥0) →ₗ[ℝ≥0] ℝ≥0. Let V̂_i := toRealPositiveLinear V_i, a positive linear functional on C_c(X, ℝ) with V̂_i(f.toReal) = V_i(f) (eq_toRealPositiveLinear_toReal).
3. (Jordan decomposition.) P_i := V̂_i + Λ_i is linear. It is positive: if k ∈ C_c(X, ℝ) satisfies k ≥ 0 then k = (nnrealPart k).toReal, so P_i(k) = V_i(nnrealPart k) + Λ_i(k) ≥ |Λ_i(k)| + Λ_i(k) ≥ 0 by 2(a). Hence P_i is a positive linear functional (monotone by linearity), and Λ_i = P_i − V̂_i.
4. (Riesz–Markov–Kakutani.) a_i := RealRMK.rieszMeasure V̂_i and b_i := RealRMK.rieszMeasure P_i are Borel measures on X, finite on compact sets (IsFiniteMeasureOnCompacts instance). They satisfy ∫ f da_i = V̂_i(f) and ∫ f db_i = P_i(f) for f ∈ C_c(X, ℝ) (RealRMK.integral_rieszMeasure). Hence Λ_i(f) = ∫ f db_i − ∫ f da_i.
5. (Dominating measure.) μ₀ := Σ_i (a_i + b_i) is finite on compact sets, being a finite sum. Hence μ₀ is σ-finite on the σ-compact space X, and so are all a_i and b_i. Since a_i ≤ μ₀ and b_i ≤ μ₀, we have a_i ≪ μ₀ and b_i ≪ μ₀ (Measure.absolutelyContinuous_of_le).
6. (Densities.) By the Lebesgue decomposition for σ-finite measures (Measure.haveLebesgueDecomposition_add, with the σ-finite instance) and Measure.singularPart_eq_zero_of_ac, a_i = μ₀.withDensity α_i and b_i = μ₀.withDensity β_i. Here α_i := a_i.rnDeriv μ₀ and β_i := b_i.rnDeriv μ₀ are measurable [0, ∞]-valued functions, finite μ₀-a.e. (Measure.rnDeriv_lt_top). For compact K, ∫⁻_K α_i dμ₀ = a_i(K) < ∞ and ∫⁻_K β_i dμ₀ = b_i(K) < ∞.
7. (The field ν.) Put ν_i(x) := (β_i x).toReal − (α_i x).toReal and ν(x) := WithLp.toLp 2 (fun i => ν_i x) ∈ H. ν is measurable, since each coordinate is and WithLp.toLp is measurable. For compact K, ‖ν(x)‖ ≤ Σ_i ((α_i x).toReal + (β_i x).toReal), and ∫_K (α_i x).toReal dμ₀ ≤ a_i(K) < ∞ (likewise for β_i). So ν is integrable on K.
8. (Scalar representation.) For f ∈ C_c(X, ℝ), ∫ f da_i = ∫ (α_i x).toReal·f(x) dμ₀(x) (integral_withDensity_eq_integral_toReal_smul; α_i is measurable and finite a.e.), and likewise for b_i. So Λ_i(f) = ∫ f(x)·ν_i(x) dμ₀(x). All these integrals are finite, because f is bounded with compact support and α_i, β_i are integrable on compact sets.
9. (Vector representation.) Let g ∈ C_c(X, H) and g_i(x) := (g x) i. Then g_i ∈ C_c(X, ℝ), being a continuous linear coordinate of g that vanishes where g does. Pointwise g(x) = Σ_i g_i(x)•e_i, so g = Σ_i g_i•e_i in C_c(X, H). Hence L(g) = Σ_i Λ_i(g_i) = Σ_i ∫ g_i ν_i dμ₀ = ∫ Σ_i g_i(x)ν_i(x) dμ₀(x) = ∫ ⟨g(x), ν(x)⟩ dμ₀(x). Each g_i ν_i is integrable, and ⟨x, y⟩ = Σ_i x_i y_i in H.
10. Hence μ₀ and ν have all the required properties.
proof_key_steps: The coordinate functionals Λ_i(f) = L(f e_i) satisfy |Λ_i f| ≤ M_K‖f‖_∞ for f supported in K.
The total variation V_i(f) = sup{Λ_i h : |h| ≤ f} is additive (clamp h between ±f₁) and homogeneous; toRealPositiveLinear turns it into a positive functional V̂_i.
P_i = V̂_i + Λ_i is positive; RMK gives Radon measures a_i, b_i with Λ_i(f) = ∫ f db_i − ∫ f da_i.
μ₀ = Σ(a_i + b_i) dominates all of them; the Lebesgue decomposition gives densities α_i, β_i, and ν_i = β_i − α_i.
L(g) = Σ_i Λ_i(g_i) = ∫⟨g, ν⟩ dμ₀.

subproblems.title: Representation T = ξ·μ with μ the mass measure (Simon 6.2.7–2.8; parent Part (REP), steps 1–5)
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (T : GeometricCurrentOn U n), IsOpen U → (∀ W : Set (Euclid P), IsOpen W → CompactlyContained W U → T.massOn W < ∞) → ∃ (μ : Measure (Euclid P)) (ξ : Euclid P → MultiVector P n), μ Uᶜ = 0 ∧ (∀ K : Set (Euclid P), IsCompact K → K ⊆ U → μ K < ∞) ∧ (∀ W : Set (Euclid P), IsOpen W → T.massOn W = μ W) ∧ AEStronglyMeasurable ξ μ ∧ (∀ (x : Euclid P) (α : Covector (Euclid P) n), |ξ x α| ≤ covectorEuclideanNorm α) ∧ (∀ ω : TestFormOn U n, T ω = ∫ x, ξ x ((ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) x) ∂μ)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof, Part (REP), steps 1–5 (Simon 6.2.7–2.8). Two substitutions are forced by the import closure of GMT.Ch07.Submission, where SimonGMT Chapter01's vector Riesz theorem (simon_theorem_4_14_caratheodory) and its positive-envelope identity (simon_theorem_4_14_positive_envelope) are unavailable. The Riesz representation of step 3 is the sibling vector_riesz, followed by an explicit polar normalization (which is what makes ‖ν‖ = 1 a.e. in the parent), and the lower mass bound of step 5 uses the sibling testform_l1_approx instead of the positive-envelope identity (3a). The extension of step 2 is the sibling testform_extension and the coefficient isometry c of the Notation paragraph is the sibling covector_euclidean_equiv. No case distinction n > P (parent step 1) is needed: the argument below is uniform in n and P (for n > P the coefficient space has dimension 0 and the construction yields μ = 0, ξ = 0).
Notation: |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α; M_W(T) := T.massOn W; val : ↥U → ℝ^P is the inclusion; H := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d).
1. (Coordinates.) By the sibling covector_euclidean_equiv choose d and c : Covector (Euclid P) n ≃L[ℝ] H with |α| = ‖c α‖. Thus |·| is a norm on covectors, and c, c⁻¹ are continuous linear.
2. (Extension.) By the sibling testform_extension (with P, n, U, T, d, c and the hypotheses) there is a linear L : C_c(U, H) → ℝ with (i) L(g) = T(ω) whenever g(x) = c(ω(x)) for all x ∈ U, and (ii) local boundedness on compact subsets of ↥U.
3. (Representation.) ↥U is locally compact (IsOpen.locallyCompactSpace), Hausdorff and second countable, and carries its Borel σ-algebra (Subtype.borelSpace). Apply the sibling vector_riesz to X := ↥U, d and L; its hypothesis is (ii). This gives a measure μ₀ on ↥U, finite on compact sets, and a measurable ν : ↥U → H, integrable on compact sets, with L(g) = ∫ ⟨g(x), ν(x)⟩ dμ₀(x) for all g ∈ C_c(U, H).
4. (Normalization and definitions.)
 - ρ(x) := ‖ν(x)‖ and ν̂(x) := ρ(x)⁻¹•ν(x), with 0⁻¹ = 0. Both are measurable, ν(x) = ρ(x)•ν̂(x) for all x, ‖ν̂(x)‖ ≤ 1, and ‖ν̂(x)‖ = 1 when ρ(x) ≠ 0.
 - μ₁ := μ₀.withDensity (x ↦ ofReal ρ(x)) on ↥U, and μ := μ₁.map val. Since U is open, hence measurable, val is a measurable embedding. So μ(A) = μ₁(val⁻¹A) for measurable A, and ∫ F dμ = ∫ F(val x) dμ₁(x) (MeasurableEmbedding.integral_map).
 - ν̂_e : ℝ^P → H is ν̂(⟨y, h⟩) for y ∈ U and 0 for y ∉ U. It is measurable, being measurable on the measurable set U and constant on Uᶜ.
 - ξ(y) := (innerSL ℝ (ν̂_e y)).comp c, so ξ(y)(α) = ⟨ν̂_e(y), c α⟩ and ξ(y) = 0 for y ∉ U.
 - β(y) := c⁻¹(ν̂_e(y)).
5. (Property 1.) μ(Uᶜ) = μ₁(val⁻¹(Uᶜ)) = μ₁(∅) = 0.
6. (Property 2.) Let K ⊆ U be compact. val⁻¹(K) is compact in ↥U, because val is an embedding and K ⊆ range val (Topology.IsInducing.isCompact_preimage_iff). So μ(K) = μ₁(val⁻¹K) = ∫⁻_{val⁻¹K} ofReal ρ dμ₀ < ∞, since ν is integrable on val⁻¹K.
7. (Properties 4 and 5.) The map Φ : H → MultiVector P n, Φ(v) := (innerSL ℝ v).comp c, is continuous linear, and ξ = Φ ∘ ν̂_e. ν̂_e is measurable into the second-countable space H, hence strongly measurable. So ξ is strongly measurable, in particular AEStronglyMeasurable for μ. For every y and α, |ξ(y)(α)| = |⟨ν̂_e(y), c α⟩| ≤ ‖ν̂_e(y)‖·‖c α‖ ≤ |α| (Cauchy–Schwarz). Likewise β = c⁻¹ ∘ ν̂_e is strongly measurable, and |β(y)| = ‖ν̂_e(y)‖ ≤ 1.
8. (Property 6.) Let ω ∈ TestFormOn U n and g_ω : ↥U → H, g_ω(x) := c(ω(val x)). g_ω is continuous. Its support is contained in val⁻¹(tsupport ω), which is compact because tsupport ω is a compact subset of U = range val. Hence g_ω ∈ C_c(U, H), and by step 2(i), T(ω) = L(g_ω). By step 3:
 L(g_ω) = ∫ ⟨c(ω x), ν x⟩ dμ₀
 = ∫ ρ(x)⟨ν̂(x), c(ω x)⟩ dμ₀(x)   (ν = ρ•ν̂, and the inner product is symmetric)
 = ∫ ⟨ν̂(x), c(ω x)⟩ dμ₁(x)   (integral_withDensity_eq_integral_toReal_smul, with (ofReal ρ).toReal = ρ)
 = ∫ ξ(val x)(ω(val x)) dμ₁(x)
 = ∫ ξ(y)(ω y) dμ(y).
9. (μ-a.e. normalization.) The set Z := Uᶜ ∪ val''{x : ρ x = 0} is measurable, and μ(Z) ≤ μ(Uᶜ) + μ₁({ρ = 0}) = 0 + ∫⁻_{ρ=0} ofReal ρ dμ₀ = 0. For y = val x ∉ Z, ξ(y)(β y) = ⟨ν̂ x, c(c⁻¹(ν̂ x))⟩ = ‖ν̂ x‖² = 1. So ξ(y)(β(y)) = 1 for μ-a.e. y.
10. (Property 3, upper bound.) Let W be open and ω ∈ massAdmissibleOn U n W. If μ(W) = ∞ there is nothing to prove. Otherwise y ↦ ξ(y)(ω y) vanishes off W (ω(y) = 0 for y ∉ tsupport ω), and |ξ(y)(ω y)| ≤ |ω y| ≤ 1. By step 8, T(ω) = ∫_W ξ(ω) dμ ≤ (μ W).toReal, so ofReal(T ω) ≤ μ(W). Taking the supremum over ω, M_W(T) ≤ μ(W).
11. (Property 3, lower bound on relatively compact pieces.) Let W be open and W' an open set with W' ⊂⊂ U and W' ⊆ W.
 - ν' := μ.restrict W' is a finite measure (μ(W') ≤ μ(closure W') < ∞ by step 6) with ν'(W'ᶜ) = 0. β is integrable for ν', being strongly measurable and bounded, and |β| ≤ 1.
 - Let ε > 0. The sibling testform_l1_approx (with P, n, ν', V := W', β, ε) gives a test form ω₀ with tsupport ω₀ ⊆ W', |ω₀| ≤ 1 and ∫⁻ ofReal|ω₀ − β| dν' < ofReal ε. Since W' ⊆ U, ω₀ defines ω ∈ TestFormOn U n, and ω ∈ massAdmissibleOn U n W because W' ⊆ W.
 - By step 8, since ω vanishes off W', T(ω) = ∫_{W'} ξ(ω) dμ = ∫_{W'} ξ(β) dμ + ∫_{W'} ξ(ω − β) dμ; both integrands are bounded on the finite-measure set W'. By step 9 the first integral is μ.real(W'). The second has absolute value ≤ ∫_{W'} |ω − β| dμ < ε, since |ξ(y)(α)| ≤ |α|.
 - Hence M_W(T) ≥ ofReal(T ω) ≥ ofReal(μ.real(W') − ε). Letting ε ↓ 0, M_W(T) ≥ μ(W').
12. (Property 3, lower bound.) Let W be open and O := W ∩ U. Since μ(Uᶜ) = 0, μ(W) = μ(O). The open set O is the increasing union of the open sets W'_j (j ≥ 1), where W'_j := ball(0, j) if O = ℝ^P, and W'_j := {y : ‖y‖ < j and infDist(y, Oᶜ) > 1/j} otherwise. The closure of each W'_j lies in the compact set {‖y‖ ≤ j, infDist(y, Oᶜ) ≥ 1/j} ⊆ O (resp. closedBall(0, j)), so W'_j ⊂⊂ U and W'_j ⊆ W. By step 11 and continuity from below, μ(W) = sup_j μ(W'_j) ≤ M_W(T).
13. Steps 5–12 give all six properties for μ and ξ.
proof_key_steps: Get the coordinates c (covector_euclidean_equiv) and the extension L of T to C_c(U, ℝ^d) (testform_extension).
vector_riesz on X = U gives μ₀ and a locally integrable ν with L(g) = ∫⟨g, ν⟩ dμ₀.
Normalize polarly: μ := val_*(|ν|μ₀) and ξ(x)(α) := ⟨ν(x)/|ν(x)|, c α⟩; this gives properties (1), (2), (4), (5) and (6).
M_W(T) ≤ μ(W) because |ξ(ω)| ≤ |ω| ≤ 1.
M_W(T) ≥ μ(W') for open W' ⊂⊂ U with W' ⊆ W, via testform_l1_approx applied to β = c⁻¹(ν/|ν|); then exhaust W ∩ U.

subproblems.title: Top-dimensional normal measures do not charge compact Lebesgue-null sets (parent step 8, Lemma TD)
subproblems.statement: Let n ∈ ℕ, let (X, ν) be a finite measure space, let q : X → ℝⁿ (Euclid n) be measurable, h : X → ℝ ν-integrable, and Λ ∈ ℝ. Assume |∫ h(x)·div g(q(x)) dν(x)| ≤ Λ for every C^∞ map g : ℝⁿ → ℝⁿ with compact support and ‖g(y)‖ ≤ 1 for all y, where div g(y) := LinearMap.trace ℝ (Euclid n) (fderiv ℝ g y). Then ∫_{q⁻¹(K)} h dν = 0 for every compact K ⊆ ℝⁿ with Lebesgue measure volume K = 0.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (n : ℕ) (X : Type) [MeasurableSpace X] (ν : Measure X) (q : X → Euclid n) (h : X → ℝ) (Λ : ℝ), IsFiniteMeasure ν → Measurable q → Integrable h ν → (∀ g : Euclid n → Euclid n, ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞) g → HasCompactSupport g → (∀ y, ‖g y‖ ≤ 1) → |∫ x, h x * LinearMap.trace ℝ (Euclid n) (fderiv ℝ g (q x)).toLinearMap ∂ν| ≤ Λ) → ∀ K : Set (Euclid n), IsCompact K → volume K = 0 → ∫ x in q ⁻¹' K, h x ∂ν = 0
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof, step 8 (Lemma TD), restricted to the case used in step 9: compact Lebesgue-null sets N, for the finite signed measure m = q_*(h ν) (so m(N) = ∫_{q⁻¹(N)} h dν). The parent derives the estimate on |∫ a dm| from the Gagliardo–Nirenberg–Sobolev inequality. That Mathlib result (eLpNorm_le_eLpNorm_fderiv_one) is not in the import closure of GMT.Ch07.Submission (verified: unknown identifier after `import GMT.Ch07.Submission`), so here the estimate is obtained by comparing a test function with its averages over balls of radius r; the remainder (smooth cut-offs of the null compact set, outer regularity of Lebesgue measure) follows the parent.
Notation:
- λ := volume on ℝⁿ = Euclid n;
- div g(y) := LinearMap.trace ℝ (Euclid n) (fderiv ℝ g y) = Σ_i ∂_i g_i(y);
- for a bounded continuous a : ℝⁿ → ℝ, F(a) := ∫ h(x)·a(q x) dν(x), which is finite since |h·(a∘q)| ≤ sup|a|·|h| and h ∈ L¹(ν);
- B_r := ball(0, r) and ‖h‖₁ := ∫|h| dν.
1. (Λ ≥ 0.) Apply the hypothesis to g = 0: 0 = |∫ h·0 dν| ≤ Λ.
2. (Directional estimate.) Let a : ℝⁿ → ℝ be C^∞ with compact support and |a| ≤ 1. We show |∫ h(x)·(a(q x + z) − a(q x)) dν(x)| ≤ Λ‖z‖ for every z ∈ ℝⁿ. This is trivial for z = 0.
 - For z ≠ 0 let w := z/‖z‖ and, for s ∈ [0, 1], g_s(y) := a(y + s z)•w. Then g_s is C^∞ with compact support and ‖g_s(y)‖ = |a(y + s z)| ≤ 1. Since fderiv g_s(y)(v) = Da(y + s z)(v)•w and the trace of v ↦ ℓ(v)•w is ℓ(w), div g_s(y) = Da(y + s z)(w). By hypothesis, |∫ h(x)·Da(q x + s z)(w) dν(x)| ≤ Λ for every s ∈ [0, 1].
 - The function s ↦ a(q x + s z) has the continuous derivative Da(q x + s z)(z). By the fundamental theorem of calculus (intervalIntegral.integral_eq_sub_of_hasDerivAt), a(q x + z) − a(q x) = ∫_0^1 Da(q x + s z)(z) ds.
 - The function (x, s) ↦ h(x)·Da(q x + s z)(z) is measurable and bounded by ‖z‖·sup‖Da‖·|h(x)|, where Da is continuous with compact support. So it is integrable on ν ⊗ (Lebesgue measure on [0, 1]).
 - By Fubini (integral_integral_swap), ∫ h(x)(a(q x + z) − a(q x)) dν(x) = ∫_0^1 ∫ h(x)·Da(q x + s z)(z) dν(x) ds = ‖z‖·∫_0^1 ∫ h(x)·Da(q x + s z)(w) dν(x) ds. Its absolute value is therefore ≤ ‖z‖Λ.
3. (Averaging estimate.) Fix r > 0 and let ψ_r := λ(B_r)⁻¹·1_{B_r}, where 0 < λ(B_r) < ∞. Then ψ_r ≥ 0, ψ_r ≤ λ(B_r)⁻¹, ∫ψ_r dλ = 1, and ψ_r = 0 off B_r. We show that for every C^∞ compactly supported a with 0 ≤ a ≤ 1, |F(a)| ≤ rΛ + λ(B_r)⁻¹‖h‖₁·∫ a dλ.
 - Since ∫ψ_r = 1, F(a) = F₁ + F₂ with F₁ := ∫ h(x) ∫ ψ_r(z)(a(q x) − a(q x + z)) dλ(z) dν(x) and F₂ := ∫ h(x) ∫ ψ_r(z)·a(q x + z) dλ(z) dν(x).
 - The integrand of F₁ is bounded by 2|h(x)|ψ_r(z), which is integrable on ν ⊗ λ. By Fubini, F₁ = −∫ ψ_r(z)(∫ h(x)(a(q x + z) − a(q x)) dν(x)) dλ(z). By step 2 and ‖z‖ < r on B_r, |F₁| ≤ ∫ ψ_r(z)Λ‖z‖ dλ(z) ≤ rΛ.
 - For each x, 0 ≤ ∫ ψ_r(z)·a(q x + z) dλ(z) ≤ λ(B_r)⁻¹∫ a(q x + z) dλ(z) = λ(B_r)⁻¹∫ a dλ, by translation invariance of λ (integral_add_right_eq_self). So |F₂| ≤ λ(B_r)⁻¹(∫ a dλ)‖h‖₁.
4. (Cut-offs.) Let K be compact with λ(K) = 0. If K = ∅ the claim is trivial, so assume K ≠ ∅. For k ∈ ℕ let O_k := thickening(1/(k+1)) K, an open set containing K. We construct a C^∞ function a_k with compact support, 0 ≤ a_k ≤ 1, a_k = 1 on K and tsupport a_k ⊆ O_k.
 - For each x ∈ K choose ρ_x > 0 with closedBall(x, 2ρ_x) ⊆ O_k, and a smooth bump φ_x centred at x with inner radius ρ_x and outer radius 2ρ_x (ContDiffBump). Then φ_x is C^∞, 0 ≤ φ_x ≤ 1, φ_x = 1 on closedBall(x, ρ_x), and support φ_x = ball(x, 2ρ_x).
 - Finitely many balls ball(x_i, ρ_{x_i}) cover K. Put a_k := 1 − Π_i(1 − φ_{x_i}). Then a_k is C^∞, 0 ≤ a_k ≤ 1, and a_k = 1 on K.
 - If a_k(y) ≠ 0 then φ_{x_i}(y) ≠ 0 for some i. So tsupport a_k ⊆ ⋃_i closedBall(x_i, 2ρ_{x_i}) ⊆ O_k, which is a compact set.
5. (Limits.)
 (i) a_k(q x) → 1_K(q x) for every x. If q x ∈ K then a_k(q x) = 1. If q x ∉ K then infDist(q x, K) > 0 (K is closed and nonempty), so q x ∉ O_k for large k and a_k(q x) = 0. By dominated convergence (|h·(a_k∘q)| ≤ |h|), F(a_k) → ∫ h(x)·1_K(q x) dν(x) = ∫_{q⁻¹(K)} h dν. Here q⁻¹(K) is measurable, since K is closed and q is measurable.
 (ii) ∫ a_k dλ ≤ λ(O_k) ≤ λ(cthickening(1/(k+1)) K) → λ(K) = 0 (tendsto_measure_cthickening_of_isCompact).
6. (Conclusion.) By steps 3 and 5, |∫_{q⁻¹(K)} h dν| = lim_k |F(a_k)| ≤ rΛ + λ(B_r)⁻¹‖h‖₁·lim_k ∫ a_k dλ = rΛ. Since r > 0 is arbitrary, ∫_{q⁻¹(K)} h dν = 0.
proof_key_steps: Λ ≥ 0, and the directional estimate |∫ h(x)(a(q x + z) − a(q x)) dν| ≤ Λ‖z‖ from the fields g_s = a(· + s z)·z/‖z‖, the fundamental theorem of calculus and Fubini.
Ball averages: |F(a)| ≤ rΛ + λ(B_r)⁻¹‖h‖₁∫a for smooth 0 ≤ a ≤ 1.
Smooth cut-offs a_k equal to 1 on K with supports in thickening(1/(k+1)) K: ∫ a_k → λ(K) = 0 and F(a_k) → ∫_{q⁻¹K} h dν.
Let k → ∞, then r → 0.

subproblems.title: Divergence identity d(b·p_I^#γ) = (b·div g∘p_I)·dx^I + db∧p_I^#γ, with bounds (parent step 9)
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P m : ℕ) (I : Fin (m + 1) → Fin P) (θ : Covector (Euclid P) (m + 1)) (b : Euclid P → ℝ), StrictMono I → (∀ v : Fin (m + 1) → Euclid P, θ v = Matrix.det (Matrix.of fun k j => v j (I k))) → ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞) b → HasCompactSupport b → ∃ K : ℝ, ∀ g : Euclid (m + 1) → Euclid (m + 1), ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞) g → (∀ y, ‖g y‖ ≤ 1) → ∃ (η : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) m) (ζ : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) (m + 1)), IsTestForm η ∧ IsTestForm ζ ∧ tsupport η ⊆ tsupport b ∧ tsupport ζ ⊆ tsupport b ∧ (∀ x, covectorEuclideanNorm (η x) ≤ K) ∧ (∀ x, covectorEuclideanNorm (ζ x) ≤ K) ∧ ∀ x, exteriorDerivative η x = (b x * LinearMap.trace ℝ (Euclid (m + 1)) (fderiv ℝ g (WithLp.toLp 2 (fun k => x (I k)))).toLinearMap) • θ + ζ x
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof, step 9. It uses three facts: p_α^#((div g) dy) = d(p_α^#γ); the Leibniz rule d(bβ) = db∧β + b dβ; and the bounds |p_α^#γ| ≤ |g| and |db∧p_α^#γ| ≤ C|db|. Here η = b·p_α^#γ with γ = Σ_j g_j ε_j is written intrinsically as η(x) = b(x)·(θ contracted with G(x)), where G = ι∘g∘p is a vector field. The constants need not be sharp.
Notation:
- n := m + 1; e_i := EuclideanSpace.single i 1 in ℝ^P; |·| := covectorEuclideanNorm; ‖·‖ is the operator norm on covectors.
- p : ℝ^P → ℝⁿ, p(x) := WithLp.toLp 2 (fun k => x (I k)), is continuous linear. ι : ℝⁿ → ℝ^P, ι(y) := Σ_k y_k•e_{I k}, is continuous linear.
- Since I is injective, p(ι(y)) = y and ‖ι(y)‖ = ‖y‖, because the e_{I k} are orthonormal.
- D(u) := det(Matrix.of fun k j => u j k) for u : Fin n → ℝⁿ. By hypothesis θ(w) = D(p ∘ w) for w : Fin n → ℝ^P.
- For a continuous alternating map α in k ≥ 1 variables and u ∈ ℝ^P, α.curryLeft u is the (k−1)-covector v ↦ α(Fin.cons u v), and ‖α.curryLeft u‖ ≤ ‖α‖‖u‖.
Facts.
(F1) For every k-covector α on ℝ^P, |α| ≤ P^k‖α‖. Each |α(e_J)| ≤ ‖α‖Π_i‖e_{J i}‖ = ‖α‖, and there are at most P^k tuples J. So |α|² ≤ P^k‖α‖², and |α| ≤ P^k‖α‖ (when P = 0 and k ≥ 1 there are no tuples and |α| = 0).
(F2) For every n-covector α, w : Fin n → ℝ^P, u ∈ ℝ^P and i ∈ Fin n: (−1)^i α(Fin.cons u (i.removeNth w)) = α(Function.update w i u). Indeed Function.update w i u = Fin.insertNth i u (i.removeNth w) (Fin.insertNth_removeNth). Moving the entry in position i to position 0 is a cyclic permutation of sign (−1)^i (AlternatingMap.map_perm, applied to the underlying alternating map of α and the cycle moving position i to position 0).
(F3) (Jacobi.) For every linear A : ℝⁿ → ℝⁿ and u : Fin n → ℝⁿ, Σ_i D(Function.update u i (A(u i))) = tr(A)·D(u).
 - Φ(u) := Σ_i D(update u i (A(u i))) is multilinear in u.
 - Φ is alternating. If u_j = u_l with j ≠ l, the terms with i ∉ {j, l} contain two equal columns and vanish. The terms i = j and i = l are exchanged by swapping columns j and l, so they cancel.
 - An alternating n-linear form on ℝⁿ equals its value at the standard basis times D (AlternatingMap.eq_smul_basis_det).
 - At the standard basis e' of ℝⁿ, D(update e' i (A e'_i)) is the determinant of the identity matrix with its i-th column replaced by A e'_i. Expanding along row i (the other rows are rows of the identity), it equals (A e'_i)_i. So Φ(e') = Σ_i (A e'_i)_i = tr(A) (LinearMap.trace_eq_matrix_trace with the standard basis).
Construction.
- Let β₀ := sup_x |b(x)| and β₁ := sup_x ‖Db(x)‖; both are finite because b and Db are continuous with compact support. Put K := (P^m·β₀ + P^n·n·β₁)·‖θ‖. K does not depend on g.
- Now let g : ℝⁿ → ℝⁿ be C^∞ with ‖g‖ ≤ 1, and let G := ι ∘ g ∘ p : ℝ^P → ℝ^P. G is C^∞, ‖G(x)‖ = ‖g(p x)‖ ≤ 1, and DG(x) = ι ∘ Dg(p x) ∘ p.
- η(x) := b(x)•θ.curryLeft(G(x)), an element of Covector (Euclid P) m.
- ζ(x) := exteriorDerivative η x − (b(x)·tr(Dg(p x)))•θ, where tr(Dg(p x)) = LinearMap.trace ℝ (Euclid n) (fderiv ℝ g (p x)).
1. (η is a test form in tsupport b.) x ↦ θ.curryLeft(G x) is C^∞, since G is C^∞ and u ↦ θ.curryLeft u is continuous linear. So η is C^∞. η(x) = 0 whenever b(x) = 0, so tsupport η ⊆ tsupport b, which is compact. Hence IsTestForm η.
2. (Derivative of η.) Fix x and w : Fin n → ℝ^P. Since η is differentiable, the exterior derivative formula (Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter06.exteriorDerivative_apply) gives exteriorDerivative η x w = Σ_i (−1)^i D_x[η(·)(i.removeNth w)](w i). Here η(y)(i.removeNth w) = b(y)·θ(Fin.cons (G y) (i.removeNth w)), and u ↦ θ(Fin.cons u v) is linear. By the product and chain rules, its derivative at x in direction w i is Db(x)(w i)·θ(Fin.cons (G x) (i.removeNth w)) + b(x)·θ(Fin.cons (DG(x)(w i)) (i.removeNth w)). Hence exteriorDerivative η x w = Z_x(w) + b(x)·S_x(w), with
 - Z_x(w) := Σ_i (−1)^i Db(x)(w i)·θ(Fin.cons (G x) (i.removeNth w));
 - S_x(w) := Σ_i (−1)^i θ(Fin.cons (DG(x)(w i)) (i.removeNth w)).
3. (S_x = tr(Dg(p x))·θ.) Let A := Dg(p x) and u := p ∘ w. By (F2), S_x(w) = Σ_i θ(update w i (DG(x)(w i))). Now θ = D(p ∘ ·), p ∘ update w i v = update (p ∘ w) i (p v), and p(DG(x)(w i)) = p(ι(A(p(w i)))) = A(u i). So S_x(w) = Σ_i D(update u i (A(u i))) = tr(A)·D(u) = tr(A)·θ(w) by (F3).
4. (ζ(x) = Z_x, and ζ is a test form in tsupport b.) By steps 2–3 and the definition of ζ, ζ(x)(w) = Z_x(w) for all w. ζ is C^∞: exteriorDerivative η is C^∞ because η is a C^∞ form, and x ↦ b(x)·tr(Dg(p x)) is C^∞ because g is C^∞ and the trace is continuous linear. If x ∉ tsupport b, then b vanishes on a neighbourhood of x, so Db(x) = 0 and ζ(x) = Z_x = 0. Thus tsupport ζ ⊆ tsupport b, which is compact, and IsTestForm ζ.
5. (Bounds.) For all x, ‖η(x)‖ ≤ |b(x)|·‖θ‖·‖G(x)‖ ≤ β₀‖θ‖. Each of the n terms of Z_x(w) is bounded by ‖Db(x)‖‖w i‖·‖θ‖‖G x‖Π_{j≠i}‖w j‖, so ‖ζ(x)‖ ≤ n·β₁‖θ‖. By (F1) with k = m and k = n, |η(x)| ≤ P^m β₀‖θ‖ ≤ K and |ζ(x)| ≤ P^n n β₁‖θ‖ ≤ K.
6. (Identity.) By the definition of ζ, exteriorDerivative η x = (b(x)·LinearMap.trace ℝ (Euclid n) (fderiv ℝ g (p x)))•θ + ζ(x) for all x, where p(x) = WithLp.toLp 2 (fun k => x (I k)).
Thus K and, for each g, the forms η and ζ have all the required properties.
proof_key_steps: Take η(x) = b(x)·θ.curryLeft(G(x)) with G = ι∘g∘p_I; it is a test form supported in tsupport b with |η| ≤ P^m sup|b|‖θ‖.
The exterior-derivative formula and the product rule split dη(x) into Z_x (the db-term) plus b(x)·S_x.
S_x = tr(Dg(p_I x))·θ by moving insertions to the front (sign (−1)^i) and Jacobi's identity Σ_i det(u with A u_i in column i) = tr(A)·det(u).
ζ := dη − (b·div g∘p_I)θ equals Z_x, vanishes off tsupport b, and is bounded by P^n·n·sup‖Db‖‖θ‖, independently of g.

subproblems.title: The mass measure of a locally normal current vanishes on Hⁿ-null sets (Simon 6.2.36; parent Part (REP), last assertion)
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (T : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (μ : Measure (Euclid P)) (ξ : Euclid P → MultiVector P n), IsOpen U → (∀ W : Set (Euclid P), IsOpen W → CompactlyContained W U → boundaryMassOn T W < ∞) → μ Uᶜ = 0 → (∀ K : Set (Euclid P), IsCompact K → K ⊆ U → μ K < ∞) → (∀ W : Set (Euclid P), IsOpen W → T.massOn W = μ W) → AEStronglyMeasurable ξ μ → (∀ (x : Euclid P) (α : Covector (Euclid P) n), |ξ x α| ≤ covectorEuclideanNorm α) → (∀ ω : TestFormOn U n, T ω = ∫ x, ξ x ((ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) x) ∂μ) → ∀ E : Set (Euclid P), μHE[n] E = 0 → μ E = 0
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof, Part (REP), last assertion (steps 6, 7, 9 and 10; Simon 6.2.36). Step 8 (Lemma TD) is supplied by the sibling top_dim_null, the form identity of step 9 together with the bounds (E2) by the sibling divergence_form, (E1) by the sibling eval_mass_bound, the coordinate covectors dx^α by the sibling coordinate_covectors, and (U1) of step 6 by Mathlib's IsOpen.ae_eq_zero_of_integral_contDiff_smul_eq_zero. The six properties of (μ, ξ) established in steps 1–5 of the parent are hypotheses here. Instead of decomposing an admissible ω into coordinates as in step 10, the proof shows ξ = 0 μ-a.e. on C and integrates.
Notation: |·| := covectorEuclideanNorm; M_W(T) := T.massOn W; Hⁿ := μHE[n]; for I : Fin n → Fin P, q_I(x) := WithLp.toLp 2 (fun k => x (I k)) ∈ ℝⁿ; 'W ⊂⊂ U' means CompactlyContained W U.
The hypotheses are referred to as:
(B) the boundary mass is finite;
(1) μ(Uᶜ) = 0;
(2) μ(K) < ∞ for compact K ⊆ U;
(3) M_W(T) = μ(W) for open W;
(4) ξ is a.e.-strongly measurable;
(5) |ξ(x)(α)| ≤ |α|;
(6) T(ω) = ∫ ξ(x)(ω(x)) dμ.
1. (n = 0.) μHE[0] = μH[0] (Measure.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_zero) and μH[0]({x}) = 1 (Measure.hausdorffMeasure_zero_singleton). If x ∈ E then 1 = μH[0]({x}) ≤ μH[0](E) = 0, which is impossible. So E = ∅ and μ(E) = 0. From now on n = m + 1. Then boundaryMassOn T W = T.boundary.massOn W =: M_W(∂T) by definition, and ∂T := T.boundary ∈ 𝒟_m(U).
2. (Compact null sets: setup.) Let C ⊆ U be compact with Hⁿ(C) = 0; we show μ(C) = 0. This is clear if C = ∅. Otherwise choose δ > 0 with cthickening δ C ⊆ U (IsCompact.exists_cthickening_subset_open) and let W := thickening(δ/2) C. W is open, C ⊆ W, and closure W ⊆ cthickening(δ/2) C, which is compact and contained in U. So W ⊂⊂ U and W ⊆ U. Then μ(W) ≤ μ(closure W) < ∞ by (2), M_W(T) = μ(W) < ∞ by (3), and M_W(∂T) < ∞ by (B).
3. (Projection of C.) Fix a strictly increasing I and an n-covector θ with θ(v) = det(Matrix.of fun k j => v j (I k)) for all v. Write q := q_I. q is linear and 1-Lipschitz, since ‖q x‖² = Σ_k x(I k)² ≤ Σ_l x(l)² = ‖x‖² for injective I. So N := q(C) is compact. On both ℝ^P and ℝⁿ, μHE[n] = c_n•μH[n] with the same constant c_n ≠ 0 (Measure.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_def, addHaarScalarFactor_volume_hausdorffMeasure_ne_zero). Hence μH[n](C) = 0. LipschitzOnWith.hausdorffMeasure_image_le (with constant 1) gives μH[n](N) ≤ μH[n](C) = 0. Hence μHE[n](N) = 0, and volume(N) = 0 by EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume.
4. (Divergence bound.) Let b : ℝ^P → ℝ be C^∞ with compact support and tsupport b ⊆ W.
 - The sibling divergence_form (with P, m, I, θ, b) gives K_b such that, for every C^∞ g : ℝⁿ → ℝⁿ with ‖g‖ ≤ 1, there are test forms η (degree m) and ζ (degree n) with tsupport η, tsupport ζ ⊆ tsupport b, |η| ≤ K_b, |ζ| ≤ K_b and exteriorDerivative η x = (b(x)·div g(q x))•θ + ζ(x). Here div g(y) := LinearMap.trace ℝ (Euclid n) (fderiv ℝ g y). Put Λ_b := K_b·(M_W(∂T).toReal + M_W(T).toReal).
 - Let g be C^∞ with compact support and ‖g‖ ≤ 1, and take η, ζ as above. Since tsupport b ⊆ W ⊆ U, they define η' ∈ TestFormOn U m and ζ' ∈ TestFormOn U n. Let ω_g := exteriorDerivativeTestOn U m η' − ζ' ∈ TestFormOn U n. Its underlying form is x ↦ (b(x)·div g(q x))•θ.
 - By linearity and GeometricCurrentOn.boundary_apply, T(ω_g) = ∂T(η') − T(ζ'). The tsupports lie in W and both masses are finite (step 2). So the sibling eval_mass_bound, applied to ∂T with W, η', r = K_b and to T with W, ζ', r = K_b, gives |∂T(η')| ≤ K_b·M_W(∂T).toReal and |T(ζ')| ≤ K_b·M_W(T).toReal. Hence |T(ω_g)| ≤ Λ_b.
 - By (6), T(ω_g) = ∫ ξ(x)((b(x)·div g(q x))•θ) dμ = ∫ b(x)ξ(x)(θ)·div g(q x) dμ(x). The integrand vanishes off tsupport b ⊆ W, so this equals ∫ h_b(x)·div g(q x) d(μ.restrict W)(x) with h_b(x) := b(x)·ξ(x)(θ).
5. (Top-dimensional lemma.) Apply the sibling top_dim_null with:
 - X := ℝ^P and ν := μ.restrict W, which is finite by step 2;
 - q, which is continuous, hence measurable;
 - h := h_b, which is a.e.-strongly measurable by (4) (evaluation at θ is continuous linear) and bounded by sup|b|·|θ| by (5), hence integrable for the finite measure ν;
 - Λ := Λ_b (step 4) and K := N (step 3).
 It gives ∫_{q⁻¹(N)} b(x)ξ(x)(θ) d(μ.restrict W)(x) = 0.
6. (Localization.) Let f := indicator(q⁻¹(N)) (x ↦ ξ(x)(θ)). f is a.e.-strongly measurable and bounded by |θ|, hence locally integrable on W for μ, because μ is finite on compact subsets of W ⊆ U by (2). For every C^∞ compactly supported b with tsupport b ⊆ W, ∫ b(x)·f(x) dμ = ∫_W b·f dμ (b vanishes off W) = ∫_{q⁻¹(N)} b(x)ξ(x)(θ) d(μ.restrict W) = 0 by step 5. By IsOpen.ae_eq_zero_of_integral_contDiff_smul_eq_zero (W open), f(x) = 0 for μ-a.e. x ∈ W. For x ∈ C we have x ∈ W and q(x) ∈ N, so f(x) = ξ(x)(θ). Hence ξ(x)(θ) = 0 for μ-a.e. x ∈ C.
7. (ξ = 0 a.e. on C.) For each strictly increasing I fix θ_I with the determinant formula (sibling coordinate_covectors, part (a)). Any θ with the same formula equals θ_I, since they agree on every v. Since Fin n → Fin P is finite, step 6 and ae_all_iff give: for μ-a.e. x ∈ C, ξ(x)(θ) = 0 for every strictly increasing I and every θ with the determinant formula for I. By part (b) of coordinate_covectors, ξ(x) = 0 for μ-a.e. x ∈ C.
8. (μ(C) = 0.) Let ω ∈ massAdmissibleOn U n W. The function y ↦ ξ(y)(ω y) vanishes outside W (ω(y) = 0 off tsupport ω ⊆ W), vanishes μ-a.e. on C (step 7), and is bounded by |ω(y)| ≤ 1 (by (5)). Hence by (6), T(ω) = ∫_{W∖C} ξ(ω) dμ ≤ μ(W∖C), which is finite, so ofReal(T ω) ≤ μ(W∖C). Taking the supremum, μ(W) = M_W(T) ≤ μ(W∖C) = μ(W) − μ(C); here C is closed, hence measurable, and μ(C) ≤ μ(W) < ∞. Thus μ(C) = 0.
9. (General E.)
 - Let E ⊆ ℝ^P with Hⁿ(E) = 0, and choose a measurable E' ⊇ E with Hⁿ(E') = 0 (exists_measurable_superset_of_null).
 - Write U = ⋃_j K_j with K_j compact: since U is open, take K_j := closedBall(0, j) if U = ℝ^P and K_j := {x : ‖x‖ ≤ j, infDist(x, Uᶜ) ≥ 1/j} otherwise.
 - Fix j. μ_j := μ.restrict K_j is finite by (2), hence locally finite and regular on ℝ^P (Measure.Regular.of_sigmaCompactSpace_of_isLocallyFiniteMeasure). So it is inner regular by compact sets on measurable sets of finite measure (MeasurableSet.exists_lt_isCompact_of_ne_top).
 - Suppose μ_j(E') > 0. Then there is a compact C ⊆ E' with μ_j(C) > 0. C ∩ K_j is a compact subset of U with Hⁿ(C ∩ K_j) ≤ Hⁿ(E') = 0, so μ(C ∩ K_j) = 0 by step 8, contradicting μ_j(C) = μ(C ∩ K_j) > 0.
 - Hence μ(E' ∩ K_j) = μ_j(E') = 0 for every j, and μ(E) ≤ μ(E') ≤ μ(Uᶜ) + Σ_j μ(E' ∩ K_j) = 0 by (1).
proof_key_steps: n = 0: μHE[0] is the counting measure, so E = ∅.
For a compact Hⁿ-null C ⊆ U pick an open W ⊂⊂ U around C; each coordinate projection q_I maps C to a compact Lebesgue-null set N.
divergence_form plus eval_mass_bound give |∫ b ξ(θ_I) div g∘q_I dμ⌞W| ≤ Λ_b uniformly in g; top_dim_null gives ∫_{q_I⁻¹N} b ξ(θ_I) dμ⌞W = 0 for all b.
Mathlib's U1 gives ξ(θ_I) = 0 μ-a.e. on C; coordinate_covectors then gives ξ = 0 μ-a.e. on C.
M_W(T) ≤ μ(W∖C) gives μ(C) = 0; inner regularity on compact pieces of U and a Borel null hull extend this to all E.
